Sources & coverage

This is a geographical reading aid, not yet an exhaustive index of every place in the two histories. Inclusion is based on a Pleiades name dated to overlap 480–323 BCE.

Greek labels use attested ancient forms and the earlier project list. Some attested forms are inflected. Where a Greek name is unavailable, the English / romanized name remains, marked †.

Modern generalized coastlines; ancient harbours and shorelines can differ. Hollow dots mark approximate representative positions.

Ancient Greece · A reading atlas

A map that unfolds as you read.

The Home view covers mainland Greece, the Aegean, Crete, and western Asia Minor. Sicily is included as an extra region for the western campaigns.

Historical scope: this edition is a broad Classical-period gazetteer. It is not yet a passage-by-passage concordance to Thucydides and the Hellenica. A dated ancient name does not by itself prove a mention in either work.

Greek names: attested ancient Greek where available; established spellings from your original city list for its entries. A † means a Greek form is missing. Use “Only places with Greek names” for a fully Greek-labelled place layer.

Geography: Natural Earth relief and generalized modern coastlines. Close zoom adds place detail; it does not turn this into a surveyed archaeological plan. Approximate gazetteer positions are shown as hollow dots.

Data snapshot: 18 September 2026. Pleiades contributors, CC BY 3.0; Natural Earth, public domain; Leaflet, BSD-2-Clause. The supplied reference PDF is not embedded or redistributed.
